reasons: Directionally correct and well-founded: Section 13.1 creates a multi-year, royalty-term-length term while Section 13.2 defers Ono's at-will exit until the later of redacted anniversaries of First Commercial Sale of both Products, so the customer has no convenience right through development, launch and early commercialization — this fails the fallback (which contemplates an available right on 60-90 days' notice) and sits in walk-away territory under the rule's 'no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term' test.

Not over-flagging: the clause is not already at the fallback (the right is unavailable for years, and the notice period is redacted so it cannot be confirmed within 30-90 days), and the finding correctly declines to flag Array's absence of a convenience right, which benefits us.

Redline is actionable and tracks the model language: at-will right available throughout the Term on thirty (30) days' notice, in whole or on a product/country basis, with refund limited to amounts prepaid for post-termination periods (not a blanket clawback of upfronts/milestones). The failed 'Customer convenience termination present' regex is a phrasing variant ('at any time ... for any reason' rather than 'for convenience'), and the >1.0 changed-character ratio reflects a rewrite the rule genuinely requires (removing the deferral trigger and inserting the notice/refund mechanics).
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position and offers the 60-90 day fallback.

Minor drafting cleanup (not a basis to reject): the retained tail 'which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination' now dangles off the refund clause rather than the notice; move it to follow 'advance written notice to Array' for clarity.
